title: Bad sight lines are the bane of my existence #yourlieinapril #theatre...
transcript: Now, I'm not gonna do a full review for your lie in April because it's closed. And frankly, there are a few positive things that I have to say about this show. Other than the fact that I hope the entire cast finds jobs after this. Because there's a lot of talent on that stage. But there are two things that I must talk about. Because I think they're very important for theater as a whole. First one being that if you are directing or designing a show, make sure that pivotal scenes are not happening in areas of the stage where there's going to be major sightline issues. Every single director needs to be following the Jessica Stone method of going all the way to the side to see what your audience is seeing. Or be like Alex Timbers and go to the back to make sure people can read those freaking hats. If we're directing a pivotal scene. And the people sitting on the side of your theater can only see 1/2 of one of the two actors in that scene, then what are we doing here? There's literally no excuse for why those scenes are happening in the back corner of a age when you have the whole stage available for it. The second aspect is the diversity in the show, which on the surface level, with an all Asian cast, looks incredible. What a Celebration. It can be great to champion diversity seen on stage, but When you champion that and yet behind the scenes on your creative team, it's still majority white. What are we doing here? If you have an all Asian cast and yet your director is white, and all of your writers, with the exception of the original Japanese book writer, are white, then what. What's. What are we. What are we really celebrating there? Like, there are Japanese people who can translate a Japanese book into English and probably better than what I had to witness in the show. I think it's important to celebrate diversity wins, but they just ring hollow when it's only the surface level. That's it. That's all I have to say about the show. Uh, really interesting concept. Some really great performances on that stage. But just the. The direction was just a huge mess. Which is too bad cause the design aesthetically looks gorgeous.
reasoning: Creator explicitly says there are few positive things to say, criticizes direction as 'a huge mess', slams sightlines and the translation, and only offers faint praise for cast talent and design aesthetics.
keyQuote: The direction was just a huge mess.
